title: Evacuation pacer and staggered regional rejoin hotfix
author: Aisha Khan
description: Context: during a regional evacuation test we observed short-lived overload spikes on healthy regions when an entire availability zone began draining. This caused cascading tenant evictions and occasional eviction-loop behavior during rejoin windows. Motivation: reduce immediate pressure on target regions during large-scale evacuations, avoid eviction loops, and prevent thundering-herd reconnects that cause SLO churn. What this PR does: 1) Introduces an evacuation pacer that envelopes node drain operations with a configurable paced timer (evacuation_pacer_ms default 500ms) so that connection handoffs and KV cache transfers are spread out across the drain window. 2) Adds a staggered regional rejoin sequencer which reintroduces nodes in small batches with backoff and health-probing to avoid large synchronous reconnect storms. 3) Fixes an eviction-loop edge case: the previous logic could mark a tenant as "stale" and immediately re-enqueue it for eviction if health metrics bounced during short rejoin probes; we now apply a short refractory period (slo_refractory_ms default 2000ms) before re-enqueuing. 4) Adds light-weight admission dampening during recovery windows (temporary token-based admission cap per-tenant) so that critical SLOs remain protected while the pool stabilizes. Migration/hardening: this implementation is feature-gated under runtime.eviction.pacer.enabled and runtime.rejoin.stagger.enabled (both disabled by default for rollouts). The default conservative pacing values are safe for production but tunable per-customer via Dedicated/Private config. Testing: unit tests (drain pacing and refractory timers), end-to-end chaos scenario replay harness (simulated AZ drain with 200 tenants), and a canary rollout to the staging region for 48 hours. Observability: new metrics added: evacuation_pacer_delay_ms.histogram, rejoin_batch_size, tenant_refractory_count, admission_dampened_tenants; traces include pacer.start/pacer.complete span tags. Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature-gate in staging for 48h. 2) Canary 5% of production ingress in a low-traffic region with telemetry watch. 3) Gradual ramp to 100% in 24-48h if SLOs remain stable. Hotfix urgency: the eviction-loop surfaced in a CS incident during customer SUP-9123 and caused visible 5xx spikes for a subset of tenants; this PR addresses the root cause and provides mitigation knobs. Checklist: - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Chaos replay scenario executed and passed - [x] Metrics and traces added - [x] Rollout plan documented - [x] Docs updated (runtime flags + tuning guide) - [x] Security review (no new secrets)

review_conversation: Diego Marquez (reviewer): The pacing queue looks good, but can we make the default pacer window configurable per-zone? Reply: yes, added zone-level override and documented config in docs/operational/evacuation_pacer.md - resolved.

Linnea Sørensen (reviewer): Concern around admission dampener accidentally throttling high-priority tenants. Reply: dampener applies token caps only during recovery windows and honors tenant priority flags; added tests and a safety-exempt list behavior - resolved.

Rahul Patel (SRE): Observability looks thin for the refractory path; suggest emitting telemetry when a tenant hits the refractory window. Reply: added tenant_refractory_count metric and tracing tag on re-enqueue decisions - resolved.
Diego Marquez: CI flaked on rejoin tests during first run. Reply: fixed race in sequencer and re-ran tests; CI now green.
merge_summary: Merged by Aisha Khan via squash-merge. Merge commit: 0a1b2c3 (squash of 6 commits). Tagged release candidate rc/evac-pacer-20260216 for canary rollout. Merge note: hotfix for SUP-9123; feature-gates off by default.
release_notes: Fixed: eviction-loop during rapid AZ drains that could re-enqueue tenants immediately and cause cascading evictions. Added: evacuation pacer to spread node drains, staggered regional rejoin sequencer to avoid reconnect storms, and admission dampener to protect SLOs during recovery. Operational: new runtime flags runtime.eviction.pacer.enabled and runtime.rejoin.stagger.enabled; see docs/operational/evacuation_pacer.md for tuning guidance.
notes_for_ops: Staging rollout review required before enabling in production. Default flags are OFF; to enable for canary set feature flag in deploy/feature_flags.yaml and monitor evacuation_pacer_delay_ms and tenant_refractory_count. If unexpected throttling occurs, disable runtime.eviction.pacer.enabled immediately and open SRE page SUP-9123.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: introduces timing changes but gated behind feature flags. Refractory logic reduces churn; admission dampener temporarily limits bursty reconnects. No data plane schema changes.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Create monitoring dashboard for rejoin_batch_size and evacuation_pacer_delay_ms; 2) Schedule 48h canary in staging; 3) Verify no increased 5xx across tenants; 4) If stable, plan gradual rollout per rollout plan.
changelog_entry: 2026-02-16: hotfix(evacuation): paced node drain and staggered rejoin to prevent eviction storms (SUP-9123)
technical_impact_summary: Introduces a timed pacer queue and per-tenant refractory window; adds lightweight per-tenant admission dampening during recovery windows. Changes are opt-in, backward compatible, and covered by unit/e2e tests. Performance overhead negligible: pacer uses non-blocking timers and batch-controlled rejoin to reduce peak CPU and KV transfer spikes.
